Canadian tech vendors are adding domestic AI hosting and regional payment rails just as federal banking regulators tighten oversight. Regulated buyers now face stricter conduct checks when deploying new automated tools.

### Domestic AI and Banking Scrutiny

Railtown AI integrated Radium's Canadian-hosted LLM APIs—Hal, Clarke, and Tycho—into Conductr and Railtracks as drop-in OpenAI and Anthropic replacements for regulated sectors. At the Canadian Institute's compliance conference, FCAC Commissioner Shereen Benzvy Miller signalled tougher oversight of algorithmic fairness and consumer vulnerability, pressing banks to upgrade model-risk governance.

Post-Series C, Float Financial is spending $5 million to open a Montréal office for its 1,000 Québec clients. A Payments Canada member ahead of Real-Time Rail, Float pairs direct pre-authorized debit with AI receipt tools where 47% of clients buy AI software.

### Ocean Pilots and Federal Tenders

Canada's [Ocean Supercluster](https://oceansupercluster.ca/) (portfolio over CAD $600 million) signed a Philippines MoU for Indo-Pacific pilots in autonomous systems, aquaculture, and port digitization. Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada also faces three upcoming tender deadlines:
- **Nov. 23:** Saskatchewan financial consultant for the Farm Debt Mediation Service.
- **Dec. 1:** Sole-source ACAN for Orbitrap ID-X Mass Spectrometer and UHPLC maintenance.
- **Dec. 2:** Multi-province SaaS system for AAFC living biological collections.
